sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: Your family feels your protection first.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You look after your family by making sure they are safe, the arrangements firm and the risks dealt with before anyone else sees them. Because care for you means strength, you find it easier to fix a problem than to say a tender thing. Your family knows they are covered, and they wait longer to hear that they are loved.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: In your first home an older relative made a point of standing on their own, and you copied it before you understood it. By your teens you had stopped asking for help, and the adults around you praised you for it.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: In your first home a sibling or a cousin stood beside you as an equal, and the two of you looked after each other. By your teens you were trusted to handle things alone, and you seldom asked an adult for help.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Since your late forties the people after you, children or younger relatives or someone you train, have measured themselves against you. They took your standards seriously, and you saw at least once that a sharp word from you stayed with them for years.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Since your late forties the people after you, children or younger relatives or someone you train, have leaned on your strength in hard moments. You gave them firm help sooner than warmth, and the warmth they did get from you counted for a great deal.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: During those years you gave your family comfort without limit, and some of them came to expect it. You spoiled the people closest to you, and you got your own ease back once others began to care for you in turn.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Distant plans crowd out home life in these years, and the people nearest to you feel the gap. What brings you back is a relative who asks plainly for your time, and you give it once you see the cost.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Household costs weigh on you in these years, and you carry more of the provision than your share. Your family notices the load in time, and you pass some of it over without losing the order you built.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The Twin at the Year Gate
sections.text: The Twin stands at your Year Gate, in plain view: your family raised you to stand on your own. You grew up in a family that praised independence, where help was earned and a capable child was noticed. Because standing on your own won you approval early, people still meet that capable face first, and they trust you to carry your share. Asking for anything has stayed the hardest thing you do, and you go without more often than anyone around you guesses.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The Twin inside the Year Gate
sections.text: The Twin lives inside your Year Gate: underneath your early years you learned to rely on yourself. As a child you learned to be your own support, in a home that expected you to manage. Because you were trusted young, you came to trust yourself before anyone else, and that steadiness has carried you through every hard year since. The habit also makes it hard for you to let people in, and you accept help only after you have tried everything alone.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The General at the Hour Gate
sections.text: The General stands at your Hour Gate, in plain view: in later life people see your authority before your warmth. You keep working under pressure in later life, and people go on bringing you the hard problems because you still take them. Because demanding work is how you know you matter, stopping feels like losing your place. Those who come after you learn your standards early and feel your sharpness as well, and they respect you more than they relax around you. Your late years carry real authority, and you hold it to the end.

sections.head: SEAT CARD

sections.text: The General lives inside your Hour Gate: your later years keep a private discipline that never quite stops. Your later life runs on habits you do not let slip, the early start and the work finished and the standard kept. Because being strong is how you feel safe, you push on past the point where others would ease off, and rest comes hard to you. The younger people around you feel protected by you more than held. Your late years stay full and demanding, and you keep your strength longer than most.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: You do your best work under real pressure.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You pick the job with the highest stakes and the tightest deadlines, and you are at your sharpest when it is going badly for everyone else. Because pressure is how you prove yourself to yourself, calm work leaves you flat and restless. What you build fastest is respect, and what you lose first is rest.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Since your late teens your reputation at work has grown out of hard moments, the emergency handled or the project rescued. You were promoted at least once for the steadiness you showed in a bad week.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Since your late teens your progress at work has come through crises, the deadline nobody could meet or the team that was falling apart. Each hard stretch left you more trusted than before, and you have rarely chosen the comfortable post.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Since your late forties you have been asked to lead in the hard moments, on boards or in crises or in work nobody else would take on. You turned down at least one easy exit because the demanding role kept you sharp.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Comfort dulled your drive at work in those years, and easy jobs held you longer than they should have. You were well liked and under-stretched, and what carried you was the skill you kept practising for pleasure.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Authority pushes back on you in these years, and a frank remark costs more than it used to. Work that is yours alone carries you through, and you do better outside a strict chain of command.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Routine tightens around your work in these years, and caution keeps you from moves that would pay more. Your reliability keeps you valued, and you find a better fit once someone else sees what you are worth.

sections.head: SEAT CARD

sections.text: The General stands at your Month Gate, in plain view: at work people see someone who can handle pressure. People at work read authority on you before you say a word, and they hand you the hard jobs early. Because you meet pressure head on, you rise fastest in work with real stakes, and the crises that break others build your name. Colleagues respect you before they warm to you, and you have learned to accept that order. Your standing in these years comes from what you carried when it was hardest.

sections.head: SEAT CARD

sections.text: The General holds your strongest seat, inside your Month Gate: your working years run on pressure you choose for yourself. You chose hard work from your late teens, the demanding course or the tough job or the role others turned down, because easy work bored you. The strain you took on built your ability faster than comfort could have, and your standing grew through it. Your body has paid for that pace in short nights and tired shoulders, and you have always recovered once you let yourself stop.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: Your friends are people who have earned it.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You keep a circle of people who have proved themselves, colleagues who stood with you when the work was hard. Because respect comes first for you, casual company bores you and light talk feels like a waste of time. Your friendships are few and serious, and the people in them stay loyal for years.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: As a child your friends were your equals, children who competed with you and stood up for you in turn. By your teens the friendships that lasted were the level ones, and you dropped the rest without a fuss.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: From your late teens your closest friends have been the people you worked hardest beside, in a tough job or a demanding team. Some acquaintances found you too intense and drifted off, and you kept the ones who stayed.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: So far your friendships have been between equals, people who never needed you to rescue them. The friends who wanted looking after drifted away, and you let them go without much regret.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Those years filled your life with lively company, friends who competed with you and pushed you on. You were at your best among a crowd of equals, and you won their respect openly.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: No seat in your Hour Gate rules Social. Since your late forties, you have seen friends less and spent more time with family and on your own, and the quiet has suited you.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Bluntness strains your friendships in these years, and some people take offence at what you meant as wit. The friends who stay value your candour, and you find them worth more than a wide circle.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: New contacts arrive faster than you can keep them in these years, and old friends drift to the edge. A small group who knew you before the busy decade keeps your footing, and you return to them again and again.

sections.head: SEAT CARD

sections.text: In later life you grow the way you always have, by taking on something difficult and holding yourself to it. sections.text: You run on adrenaline through long weeks and notice the tiredness only when the pressure lifts. sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: You love best as an equal, or not at all.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You fall for people with their own opinions and their own plans, and you lose interest in anyone who needs you to lead. Because a matched partner makes you feel safe, you argue as an equal and keep count of who gave way last. You find it harder to be carried by a partner, even for a day, than to win any argument.

sections.text: Your money rises and falls with each decade.

sections.text: Your finances follow no single pattern from birth. Some stretches of years bring money in and others drain it, and you feel the difference each time the decade turns.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Competition sharpened your earning in those years, and you went after money that others wanted too. You won your share by working beside rivals, and you learned exactly what your effort was worth.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Chances multiply in these years and spread you thin, with more deals in view than you can follow. One reliable source keeps paying while the others rise and fall, and you come through with your savings intact.

sections.head: COMING

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You think best out loud, with one person close enough to hear the rough version and sharp enough to push back. Because your ideas only feel real once they have been tested on someone, an evening of silence at home leaves you restless. You give your partner your best ideas first, and your harshest opinions too.

Because you need to know where you stand, open-ended jobs leave you uneasy, and a proper title settles you. What you gain is lasting rank, and what you lose is the freedom to move quickly.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE · the pair line

sections.text: Since your late teens you have been promoted by people who trusted you early, a manager or a mentor who put your name forward. Your references have opened doors for you more than once, and you have rarely had to ask for a step up.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Ambition softens in these years, and the easy option keeps winning at work. What you make still has value, and you move forward each time a deadline or a client gives you a reason to finish.

sections.head: COMING

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: Your body follows the mood of your home.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You sleep well and eat well in a settled house, and both slip the moment it turns tense. Your energy is highest in the seasons you feel most looked after.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Good care kept you well in those years, with regular meals, early nights and someone who noticed when you were tired. You recovered quickly from strain, and you felt safe in your body.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: Your family grows louder, and dearer, with age.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You are pulled toward the strong-willed people in your family, the ones who push back and want their share. Because you respect whoever stands up to you, you give most to whoever argues hardest, and the quieter ones get less of you. You love a full and noisy table more than a calm one.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: In your first home there were clear rules and an older relative who held everyone to them. By your teens you knew exactly what the family expected of you, and you met most of it while keeping a few doubts to yourself.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED

sections.text: The Sage holds your strongest seat, inside your Month Gate: your working years are carried by steady learning. Your working years rest on what you know, and you keep adding to it long after others stop studying. Because learning is how you feel safe, you prepare thoroughly for everything, and you wait to feel ready before you put yourself forward. Your ability has outrun your confidence for years, and the people who taught you have seen it sooner than you have. You gain your place slowly, and it lasts because it was built on trust.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: Your circle is full of rivals you respect.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: Most of your friends come from work, and many of them started as people you competed against. Because you respect anyone who can beat you, your closest bond at work is with a former rival. You lose friends over contests more easily than most people, and you keep the ones who competed fairly.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: From your late teens you have made friends through competition, in teams and offices and courses where everyone was ranked. More than once a friendship ended when you won, and you have kept the rival who took a loss well.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: So far your friendships have been between equals, people who never needed you to rescue them. The friends who wanted looking after drifted away, and you let them go without much regret.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Respect came to you in those years through how you conducted yourself among others. People saw you as fair and dependable, and you were asked to lead more than once.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: No seat in your Hour Gate rules Social. Since your late forties, you have seen friends less and spent more time with family and on your own, and the quiet has suited you.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: You widen your circle in these years, through travel and new groups and people met through other people. You make more new friends in this decade than in the two before it.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: You become more outspoken in these years, and the people who like it like it a great deal. You gather an audience of your own, and you lose patience with company that asks you to be quieter.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The Rival at the Month Gate
sections.text: The Rival stands at your Month Gate, in plain view: at work people see your nerve before anything else. The working world sees your competitive side first, the colleague who volunteers whenever there is a contest to enter. Because winning in the open is how you prove your worth, you rise fastest where results are ranked and stall where credit is pooled. You make allies quickly and lose them almost as quickly, and your worst setbacks have come through bets you shared with someone else.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The Twin inside the Day Gate
sections.text: The Twin lives inside your Day Gate, the seat of your partner: you love as an equal, and only as an equal. At close range you need a partner who stands as tall as you, and you have never stayed long with someone who leans. Because equality is how you feel respected, your home runs with two people deciding and neither one in charge. The cost is a quiet tally of who did what, kept by both of you and spoken by neither. From your mid-thirties your private life settles around one level bond, and you grow easier about being looked after inside it.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: You learn steadily, and it never stops.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: Week by week you add to what you know, studying in a steady and patient way. Because understanding a thing fully is what makes you feel secure, you read the extra chapter and take the extra course, and you rarely feel finished. You know far more than you claim to.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: As a child you had books at home and adults who answered your questions, and school came easily. By your teens a teacher or older relative had taken a special interest in you, and you worked harder because of it.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: From your late teens learning carried you, through courses and qualifications and the teachers who took an interest. You have stayed a student in some form ever since, and it has kept you steadier than the people around you.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: You turned inward in those years, into subjects few people around you shared. You spent long stretches alone with your thinking, and some of it still feels like the most important work you have done.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: No seat in your Hour Gate rules Mind. Since your late forties, you have thought less about ideas and more about people and daily life, and your curiosity has turned practical.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: You turn your thinking outward in these years, and you say in public what you used to keep to yourself. You are quicker and bolder with ideas than at any time before.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The Sage at the Year Gate
sections.text: The Sage stands at your Year Gate, in plain view: your childhood showed the world that you were well protected. You were raised by someone with principles, and the protection of those years shows in how you carry yourself. Because learning was valued where you grew up, teachers took to you early, and help arrived each time you needed it. People still read you as someone who was well brought up, and older people trust you on sight. You expect shelter to appear when things go wrong, and you are slower than most to build your own.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: Your money finds new openings late in life.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You notice a chance to earn where others see an ending, a late venture or a deal offered by someone younger. Because new money excites you more than kept money, you give generously and write down too little of it. Your plans live in your head far longer than they live on paper.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE · the pair line
sections.text: You lose money most easily where you share it with friends and family, and you also find your safety net among those same people. They share one gate in you, and you rarely own anything that is only yours.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Since your late forties money has reached you through new ventures and unexpected offers, at least once from a direction you had stopped watching. You have given a good share of it away, more than once without noting to whom.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: You turn steady work into something you own in these ten years, a home or savings or a share in something lasting. You keep more of what you earn than in any decade before it.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: A Horizon decade, lining up with the Horizon in your Hour Gate. It is the strongest stretch for your money in your chart. Money comes to you through openings in these years more than through salary, a deal or a side venture or a move. You take more chances with money than you did ten years earlier, and most of them pay.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The Horizon at the Hour Gate
sections.text: The Horizon stands at your Hour Gate, in plain view: people see your later years as busy with new chances and new ventures. Others see you finding new chances long after most people have settled, and younger people seek you out because of it. Since a fresh start keeps you sharp, you take on a new field or a new venture when people your age are winding down. Your generosity runs years past your written plans, and you give the people after you more stories than records.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: Your body trusts food and rest to put it right.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You trust your body to fix itself with a good meal and a long sleep, and for most of your life it has. Because comfort is how you recover, you reach for it under stress, and you turn the extra helping or the lost weekend into a habit before you notice. Your body asks you for rhythm more than for effort.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: You were a child who recovered quickly, from colds and falls and bad days alike. Your appetite and your sleep were steady, and you came into adulthood with more reserve than most of the people around you.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: No seat in your Hour Gate rules Health. Since your late forties, you have given your attention to others and to work more than to your body, and your energy has followed the decade you are in.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Your body answered strain well in those years, and hard training or hard work made you stronger. You had energy for demanding days, and you recovered fast between them.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: An Artisan decade, lining up with the Artisan in your Year Gate. It is the strongest stretch for your body in your chart. You ease into your body in these years, with better appetite and better sleep and more pleasure in ordinary days. You enjoy your health in this decade more than you have since childhood.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The Artisan inside the Year Gate
sections.text: The Artisan lives inside your Year Gate: underneath your early years were comfort and care, given freely. You were fed well as a child, in more than one sense, and that early comfort still sits under the way you live. Because ease was given to you before you had to earn it, you recover through simple things, food and a full night's sleep and the company of people you love. Whatever else your first home held, you took from it a store of warmth you have drawn on in every hard season since.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: Your family looks after you, and you let it.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You are cared for by younger people more than you expected, with visits and help and small kindnesses. Because you are used to being the one who gives, you wave off help you need, and it hurts the people offering. What you want from your family now is company more than help.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: An older relative in your first home, a father or someone who stood in for one, spent widely and drew people around them. By your teens you had learned both the warmth of that generosity and what it cost the household.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Someone in your first home looked after you closely, a parent or an older relative whose calm you came to rely on. By your teens you expected the world to treat you with the same care, and mostly it did.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Since your late forties you have become the relative who hosts, the one whose home the younger ones head for at holidays. Children or younger relatives or someone you train have picked up your habits of giving, and you see yourself in how they treat their own guests.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Since your late forties the people around you have started looking after you in small ways, a lift or a meal or a phone call that comes unasked. You have found it harder to accept than to give, and you have learned to say yes more often.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Order and good manners shaped your home in those years, and you knew your place and your duties. You earned respect from older relatives by keeping the family's rules, and you felt secure inside them.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: A Sage decade, lining up with the Sage in your Hour Gate. It is the stretch that asks most of your family. Family protection turns heavy in these years, and help arrives with conditions attached. You stay grateful and still find your own way, and the bond survives the distance you need.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The Horizon at the Year Gate
sections.text: The Horizon stands at your Year Gate, in plain view: your first home spent openly on people and on chances. You grew up in a family that spent on guests, gifts and new plans, and everyone around you could see it. Because money moved freely in the house you grew up in, you learned to spot a chance quickly and to hold cash loosely. That ease with risk has served you all your life, and you have had to build for yourself the savings habit your family never taught.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The Sage inside the Year Gate
sections.text: The Sage lives inside your Year Gate: underneath your childhood was real care, steady enough to trust. Real care sits underneath your early years, from someone whose steadiness became the way you meet the world. Because someone took good care of you, you trust people first, and protectors keep turning up when you need them. The same safety made leaving it hard, and you have stayed in comfortable places longer than they helped you. You still recover from hard seasons by going back to the people who love you.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The Artisan at the Hour Gate
sections.text: The Artisan stands at your Hour Gate, in plain view: your later years are known for what you make and give. You make things and give them away more freely in later life than at any earlier time, and the younger people around you carry your skills and your generosity with them. Because making and giving are how you feel useful, you spend those years making things for the pleasure of it and teaching what your hands know. You enjoy those years more than most people do, and the one thing that slows your work is comfort that asks nothing of you.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The Sage inside the Hour Gate
sections.text: The Sage lives inside your Hour Gate: underneath your later years is a quiet store of care, given back. Your later life rests on kindness you gave years before, and it comes back to you as care from those you helped. Because you spent decades looking after others, accepting help feels strange to you, and you learn it slowly. Your days settle into gentle routines of reading, rest and good company. A life with no strain grows small, and you feel it most in the seasons when nobody asks anything of you.

sections.text: You are trusted at work because you know your subject properly, and people check their facts with you. Because depth matters more to you than visibility, you leave the self-promotion to others, and promotion reaches you later than it should. Your standing grows slowly and holds when louder careers fall away.

sections.text: Since your late forties your work has turned toward teaching, hosting or finishing projects you had put off for years. Some of what you have made in this stretch has been better received than anything from your busier decades, and you have been surprised by it.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Promotion came the proper way in those years, through good work noticed by the right people. You earned a title you could be proud of, and you wore the responsibility well.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: You take on hard assignments and real pressure in these years, and you rise because of them. You come out of the decade with more authority than you went in with.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Your career wanders in these years between study and side projects, and steady output is hard to keep up. What carries you is one skill you can sell, and you return to it whenever money runs short.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Office rivalry eats your energy in these years, and a shared project costs you more than it pays. Your own work stays visible all the same, and the people who matter see that you did it.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: People at work either love you or resist you.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: Your circle at work splits quickly into people who champion you and people who resent you, with few in between. Because being remembered matters more to you than being liked, you say the sharp thing in meetings and lose a friend or two to it. Your loyal few have done more for your name than general approval could, and you keep them close for years.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: As a child you were the one other children wanted to sit next to, and adults made a fuss of you at every gathering. By your teens you already had more friends than you could keep up with, and you were invited everywhere.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: From your late teens your friendships have formed around strong reactions, people who liked your edge at once or never warmed to it. More than once a friendship ended over something you said in public, and you have kept every friend who stayed through it.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: So far your friendships have been between equals, people who never needed you to rescue them. The friends who wanted looking after drifted away, and you let them go without much regret.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: No seat in your Hour Gate rules Social. Since your late forties, you have seen friends less and spent more time with family and on your own, and the quiet has suited you.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Respect came to you in those years through how you conducted yourself among others. People saw you as fair and dependable, and you were asked to lead more than once.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: You widen your circle in these years, through travel and new groups and people met through other people. You make more new friends in this decade than in the two before it.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The Artisan at the Year Gate
sections.text: The Artisan stands at your Year Gate, in plain view: warmth and easy charm were the first things people saw in you. You were a warm, easy child, and the older relatives around you noticed it before anything else. Because affection came to you early and without effort, people have welcomed you and let you off lightly all your life. Your health has held up on regular meals and sleep more than on effort, and you feel the seasons of excess later than others do.

sections.text: The Virtuoso stands at your Month Gate, in plain view: at work you are seen as gifted and hard to manage. Your talent is the first thing colleagues see, and your patience with rules is the last. Because you need your work to be seen and judged fairly, you shine under bosses who reward results and stall under bosses who want obedience. Your name in your working years is built on visible wins, and you have walked away from at least one job that wanted you quieter.

sections.head: SEAT CARD

sections.text: The Twin lives inside your Day Gate, the seat of your partner: you love as an equal, and only as an equal. At close range you need a partner who stands as tall as you, and you have never stayed long with someone who leans. Because equality is how you feel respected, your home runs with two people deciding and neither one in charge. The cost is a quiet tally of who did what, kept by both of you and spoken by neither. From your mid-thirties your private life settles around one level bond, and you grow easier about being looked after inside it.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: Your mind runs best on what others find strange.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You think best alone, on problems other people have given up on or never noticed. Because you trust only the conclusions you reached alone, you rework a problem long after others have moved on, and you find small talk harder than hard questions. You keep most of what you know to yourself, and it is often the thing that matters most.

sections.text: From your late teens your mind went its own way, into a subject or a method most people around you did not follow. You have spent more nights with a question than with company, and you would not trade them back.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: You grow late, and mostly in private.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You grow in long quiet stretches that look like standing still, and then you change all at once. Because you change on the inside first, the people around you often underrate where you are, and you let them. You are further along than anyone watching would guess.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: You grew in those years by going your own way, often away from what was expected of you. The progress was real and nearly invisible, and you felt behind while you made it.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Since your late forties you have found yourself explaining things you once took for granted, and it has taught you as much as it taught others. You have written down or passed on more of what you know than in all the years before.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: Your work pays for what only you know.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You are the specialist people call when the usual answers fail. Because you trust knowledge you have dug out yourself, you are drawn to a narrow field the mainstream ignores, and you would rather be paid for strange work than praised for ordinary work. You earn more from the niche you choose than any ladder would pay you.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: Your money grows quietly from early habits.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You save without thinking about it, a little from everything, and spending without a reason feels wrong to you. Because careful habits were normal in your first home, you build wealth slowly and steadily, and few people notice until it is large. You enjoy keeping money more than spending it, and a big purchase stays on your mind for weeks.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE · the pair line
sections.text: You lose money most easily where you share it with friends and family, and you also find your safety net among those same people.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: By your teens you were already saving, keeping coins or small earnings longer than your friends did. You learned as a child that money kept quietly was money that stayed, and you have kept that habit.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Cash slipped through your hands in those years, lent to friends or spent keeping up with them. You learned what generosity costs, and what carried you was work you could do on your own.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: No seat in your Hour Gate rules Wealth. Since your late forties, you have cared more about the people after you and your own time than about earning more, and your money has held level.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: A Steward decade, lining up with the Steward in your Year Gate. It is the strongest stretch for your money in your chart. You turn steady work into something you own in these ten years, a home or savings or a share in something lasting. You keep more of what you earn than in any decade before it.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Money comes to you through openings in these years more than through salary, a deal or a side venture or a move. You take more chances with money than you did ten years earlier, and most of them pay.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The Steward inside the Year Gate
sections.text: The Steward lives inside your Year Gate: underneath your first years lay a careful home where nothing was wasted. You took in your family's careful habits with money before you could name them, and they still shape how you feel about spending. Because thrift felt like safety when you were small, you save quietly and early, and your money grows in ways other people mistake for luck. Your relatives remain the people you turn to first, and they turn to you. Under the calm sits a small worry about running short, and you carry it even in good years.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: You were born with a forgiving body.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You recover quickly from big meals and short nights, and your body has rarely let you down. Because pleasure has never felt dangerous to you, you let the treats and the late nights pile up until your energy drops. A steady routine of food and rest puts you right, and you feel well again within a week of going back to it.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE · the pair line
sections.text: In your heaviest thinking seasons you also forget to eat and sleep properly, and your body tells you before your mind admits it.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: You ate well and slept soundly in your first years, and a bad day or a cold never kept you down for long. Food at home was a pleasure more than a rule, and by your teens you loved a good meal more than most of your friends did.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: You were looked after closely in those years, and you learned to rest only when someone told you to. Your body got used to care coming from outside, and you had to learn later to give it to yourself.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED

sections.head: COMING

sections.text: Week by week you add to what you know, studying in a steady and patient way. Because understanding a thing fully is what makes you feel secure, you read the extra chapter and take the extra course, and you rarely feel finished. You know far more than you claim to.

sections.text: By your teens you had seen that money in your family came through moving, a relative working away or a business that travelled. The first money you made yourself came from beyond your own neighbourhood, and you liked how that felt.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Competition sharpened your earning in those years, and you went after money that others wanted too. You won your share by working beside rivals, and you learned exactly what your effort was worth.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Since your late forties people have turned to you for support, younger relatives and friends with plans that needed money. You have said yes more often than you meant to, and you have seen some of it pay off and some of it disappear.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Chances multiply in these years and spread you thin, with more deals in view than you can follow. One reliable source keeps paying while the others rise and fall, and you come through with your savings intact.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Caution about money tightens in these years, and spending on yourself starts to feel wrong. You have more put by than you feel you have, and you relax a little each time you check.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The Horizon inside the Year Gate
sections.text: The Horizon lives inside your Year Gate: underneath your settled surface sits a pull toward somewhere else, carried down your family. Somewhere in your family a relative left home to look for something better, and that restlessness lives on quietly in you. Because moving was part of how your family got by, you feel most alive in unfamiliar places and most at rest when you come back. Your best chances come from far off, and you have always needed a fixed home to return to.

sections.text: The Rival stands at your Hour Gate, in plain view: in later life people see your nerve and ask you to back them. Your later years stay bold and public, with people coming to you for backing long after others have stopped taking risks. Because being in the contest keeps you feeling alive, you say yes to the young and the daring more than you planned. You find real joy in some of that backing, and you lose part of what you give to people who only wanted the money.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: Your family trusts your word completely.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You look after your family by keeping everything in order, the papers sorted and the promises kept. Because reliability is how you express love, you are more at ease arranging things for people than talking about feelings. Your family depends on that order, and they know less of your heart than of your plans.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: As a child you heard about a relative who had moved away, or you moved yourself and learned to make friends quickly. By your teens your family stretched across more than one place, and you felt at home in each of them.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Since your late forties the people after you, children or younger relatives or someone you train, have relied on your word without checking it. You have settled matters for them quietly and in good time, and few of them have seen how much you handled.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Family rules weighed on you in those years, and you lived up to expectations that left you little say. You did your duty well, and the discipline it taught you later gave you a voice of your own.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Distant plans crowd out home life in these years, and the people nearest to you feel the gap. What brings you back is a relative who asks plainly for your time, and you give it once you see the cost.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Household costs weigh on you in these years, and you carry more of the provision than your share. Your family notices the load in time, and you pass some of it over without losing the order you built.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Indulgence runs the household in these years, with treats, late meals and little order. The warmth survives while your family learns to look after itself, and you stop wearing yourself out to please them.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: Your friends bring you their troubles.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You become the friend people confide in, the calm one who listens and gives sound advice. Because being trusted feels like a kind of care to you, you rarely say no, and your evenings fill with other people's problems. You find it hard to ask for the same help yourself.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: As a child you were popular with other children and with adults, and you were invited everywhere. By your teens you had a wide circle and one or two close friends who mattered far more, and you knew which were which.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Since your late teens you have been the one friends and colleagues come to when something goes wrong. You have kept more confidences than you can count, and few people have asked how you were doing in return.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: So far your friendships have been between equals, people who never needed you to rescue them. The friends who wanted looking after drifted away, and you let them go without much regret.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Your circle spread wide in those years, through travel, work and friends of friends. You met people easily everywhere you went, and several of them opened doors for you.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Since your late forties your name has carried weight in your circle, and you have been asked to lead groups you once simply belonged to. You gained respect that outlasted any title, and you found yourself consulted on matters well outside your old work.

sections.head: COMING

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: Your work is only as good as your sleep.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: Your body and your work move together, and both run best on regular meals, real rest and a steady routine. Because pleasure in food and rest comes easily to you, comfort slips into excess in your busiest months and your energy drops. You notice tiredness in the quality of your work before you feel it, and a few good nights of sleep put it right.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: As a child you were looked after well whenever you were tired or run down, and you got your energy back quickly. By your teens you had a steady energy the adults around you counted on, and you have kept much of it since.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Since your late teens your energy has followed your routine closely, high in the months you slept and ate well and flat when either slipped. At least once a long stretch of hard work wore you down, and you came back from it through rest more than effort.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Comfort turned into excess in those years, with rich food, late nights and too little effort. Your energy dropped as the easy habits piled up, and what carried you back was a plain daily routine.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Since your late forties your sleep has deepened and your appetite has steadied, and you have enjoyed your food without guilt. Your energy has dipped in the stretches when you were on your own too much, and it has come back each time the house filled up again.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: You carry more pressure in these years, and for once it suits your body. You are fitter and sharper in a demanding decade than in an easy one, and you stay that way while you keep sleeping.

sections.head: SEAT CARD

sections.text: The Sage lives inside your Year Gate: underneath your childhood was real care, steady enough to trust. Real care sits underneath your early years, from someone whose steadiness became the way you meet the world. Because someone took good care of you, you trust people first, and protectors keep turning up when you need them. The same safety made leaving it hard, and you have stayed in comfortable places longer than they helped you. You still recover from hard seasons by going back to the people who love you.

sections.text: The Artisan holds your strongest seat, inside your Month Gate: your working years run on steady craft and a body kept well. You do your work steadily and without fuss, and over your working years you quietly produce more than people who make more noise. Because your energy comes from sleep, food and routine, your work rises and falls with how well you are living. Careers in making or feeding or teaching suit you best, and you improve at them long after others have peaked.

sections.head: SEAT CARD

sections.text: The Artisan lives inside your Hour Gate: your later life settles into good food, deep sleep and people who keep coming back. Your life grows easier with age, and the comfort you have worked for becomes yours to enjoy after your late forties. Because care for you has always meant a good meal and a warm bed, your later home fills with younger people and old friends. Ease is both the reward of those years and their one risk, and you stay well for as long as your days keep a rhythm.

You are seldom the loudest on a team, and your work is the work that holds up.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: Your money comes in strong seasons and quiet ones.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You earn in bursts, a run of good months and a quiet stretch after. Because each good season makes you sure of the next, you spend the winnings on a new chance before you have kept any. You are richer in the middle of each lucky stretch than after it.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE · the pair line
sections.text: What you make turns into money more easily for you than for most, and you earn most from the work that feels like play. They share one gate in you, and you are paid in the same season that you make.

sections.text: Partnerships and shared ventures pay in these ten years, because the contest with others pushes you harder. You earn more with people at your side than alone, and you keep a fair part of what you win together.

sections.head: TITLE

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You keep your household running, the cupboards full and the bills paid before they are due. Because a well kept home is how you show love, you feel uneasy when things at home are left undone. Your family feels safe without knowing how much you do, and you rarely tell them.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: As a child you heard about a relative who had moved away, or you moved yourself and learned to make friends quickly. By your teens your family stretched across more than one place, and you felt at home in each of them.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: So far you have been the one who keeps the home in order, wherever you have lived. Your family and friends have turned to your household in hard weeks, and you have always made space for them.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: In those years you kept your own counsel at home and asked your family for very little. The distance grew quietly, and what carried you was the one relative who treated you as an equal.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Since your late forties younger members of your family have come to you with their problems, and you have taken real care over each one. At least once you have protected someone younger at a cost to yourself, and you would do it again.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Since your late forties your family has come to include people you chose, old friends with a key and younger relatives who treat you as their match. You have kept that circle small on purpose, and you have seen less of relatives who treated you as fragile.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: These ten years bring a softer household, with shared meals and unhurried weekends. You make the home a comfortable place, and relatives come to you because it feels good to be there.

sections.text: The Horizon lives inside your Year Gate: underneath your settled surface sits a pull toward somewhere else, carried down your family. Your best chances come from far off, and you have always needed a fixed home to return to.

sections.text: The Sage stands at your Hour Gate, in plain view: in later life you are seen as the one who teaches and protects. sections.text: The Sage stands at your Year Gate, in plain view: your childhood showed the world that you were well protected. You were raised by someone with principles, and the protection of those years shows in how you carry yourself. Because learning was valued where you grew up, teachers took to you early, and help arrived each time you needed it. People still read you as someone who was well brought up, and older people trust you on sight. You expect shelter to appear when things go wrong, and you are slower than most to build your own.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: You choose a small circle and keep it close.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You prefer a handful of people who really know you to a wide circle who only recognise you. Because you open up slowly, the friends you keep have earned it, and they tell you things they tell nobody else. You find parties tiring and long talks restoring.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: As a child you stood at the edge of groups for a long time, and other children took a while to warm to you. By your teens you had one or two close friends who understood you, and you needed nobody else.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: During those years you held yourself apart from most groups, sure that few people matched your standard. Your circle shrank to one or two, and you found those one or two were enough.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: No seat in your Hour Gate rules Social. Since your late forties, you have seen friends less and spent more time with family and on your own, and the quiet has suited you.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Comparison runs through your friendships in these years, and you notice who earns more and who wins more. What carries you is one friend who never competes with you, and you lean on that friend often.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: You become more outspoken in these years, and the people who like it like it a great deal. You gather an audience of your own, and you lose patience with company that asks you to be quieter.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: You widen your circle in these years, through travel and new groups and people met through other people. You make more new friends in this decade than in the two before it.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The Alchemist at the Year Gate
sections.text: The Alchemist stands at your Year Gate, in plain view: as a child you were seen as watchful, deep and a little apart. You were the child who watched before joining in, and adults noticed how differently you learned. Because you took in the world on your own terms, adults found you older than your years and other children found you hard to read. That early difference became the way people still see you, thoughtful and selective and slow to open up. You keep a few close friends in place of a crowd, and you have never regretted the trade.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: Your warmth opens doors for you.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: People warm to you on first meeting, and they remember how you made them feel long after the talk itself. Since being liked was your first way of belonging, you give more than you take in every circle you join, through hosting and small kindnesses. Your friends are many and loyal, and you show your worries to very few of them.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: As a child you were the one other children wanted to sit next to, and adults made a fuss of you at every gathering. By your teens you already had more friends than you could keep up with, and you were invited everywhere.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Your sharp tongue cost you friends in those years, and a few groups closed ranks against you. You kept the people who liked your honesty, and those few saw you through.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: No seat in your Hour Gate rules Social. Since your late forties, you have seen friends less and spent more time with family and on your own, and the quiet has suited you.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: New contacts arrive faster than you can keep them in these years, and old friends drift to the edge. A small group who knew you before the busy decade keeps your footing, and you return to them again and again.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Duty shapes your friendships in these years, and social life starts to feel like obligation. Your good name holds, and you find relief with the friends who expect nothing formal from you.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The Artisan at the Year Gate
sections.text: The Artisan stands at your Year Gate, in plain view: warmth and easy charm were the first things people saw in you. You were a warm, easy child, and the older relatives around you noticed it before anything else. Because affection came to you early and without effort, people have welcomed you and let you off lightly all your life. Your health has held up on regular meals and sleep more than on effort, and you feel the seasons of excess later than others do.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: You keep starting new things when others stop.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You grow by entering fields you know nothing about, at an age when most people stick to what they know. Because being a beginner keeps you awake and curious, a life that only repeats itself bores you within months. You surprise the people around you with how many times you begin again.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE · the pair line
sections.text: You grow most through the years that weigh on you, and you have left every heavy stretch more skilled than you entered it.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Your progress in those years came from peers who were your equals, people you learned beside more than beneath. You set your own standard and met it, and the confidence lasted.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Since your late forties you have taken up at least one new field, a subject or a trade or a kind of work nobody expected from you. Younger company has kept you learning in those years, and you have looked less settled than people your age.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Setbacks arrive in these years without warning, and you are pushed before you feel ready. What carries you is the discipline you already have, and you end the decade tougher in ways that show later.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The Horizon at the Hour Gate
sections.text: The Horizon stands at your Hour Gate, in plain view: people see your later years as busy with new chances and new ventures. Others see you finding new chances long after most people have settled, and younger people seek you out because of it. Since a fresh start keeps you sharp, you take on a new field or a new venture when people your age are winding down. Your generosity runs years past your written plans, and you give the people after you more stories than records.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: You learned the value of money early.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You spend with a list and save before anyone asks you to, and money that sits unplanned makes you uneasy. Because order around money felt like safety from your first years, you lose more sleep over a careless purchase than it ever cost you. You are slower to enjoy what you have than to keep it.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE · the pair line
sections.text: What you make turns into money more easily for you than for most, and you earn most from the work that feels like play.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: You learned what things cost before most children do. Money at home was counted and spent with care, and by your teens you were already saving what your friends spent.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Competition sharpened your earning in those years, and you went after money that others wanted too. You won your share by working beside rivals, and you learned exactly what your effort was worth.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: No seat in your Hour Gate rules Wealth. Since your late forties, you have cared more about the people after you and your own time than about earning more, and your money has held level.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: A Steward decade, lining up with the Steward in your Year Gate. It is the stretch that asks most of your money. Caution about money tightens in these years, and spending on yourself starts to feel wrong. You have more put by than you feel you have, and you relax a little each time you check.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Chances multiply in these years and spread you thin, with more deals in view than you can follow. One reliable source keeps paying while the others rise and fall, and you come through with your savings intact.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The Steward at the Year Gate
sections.text: The Steward stands at your Year Gate, in plain view: your first home ran on care, counting and things kept. You grew up where money was spoken about plainly and spent with a plan, and that order was the first thing people saw in your family. Because care with money reached you as safety, you still feel calm when the accounts are in order and uneasy when they are not. You still run every budget on the habits you formed before sixteen, and they are why your savings grow when others stall.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: Your money grows quietly from early habits.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You save without thinking about it, a little from everything, and spending without a reason feels wrong to you. Because careful habits were normal in your first home, you build wealth slowly and steadily, and few people notice until it is large. You enjoy keeping money more than spending it, and a big purchase stays on your mind for weeks.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE · the pair line
sections.text: You turn money into position, and you feel richer when a gain comes with respect than when it comes alone.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: As a child you watched money arrive in good months and go out on visitors and fresh ideas. By your teens you had a quick eye for a chance and very little saved, and both habits stayed.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: By your teens you were already saving, keeping coins or small earnings longer than your friends did. You learned as a child that money kept quietly was money that stayed, and you have kept that habit.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Careful earning paid off in those years, and you saved steadily from regular work. You built up something solid without luck or risk, and you trusted your own counting more than any tip.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: No seat in your Hour Gate rules Wealth. Since your late forties, you have cared more about the people after you and your own time than about earning more, and your money has held level.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Other people reach for your money in these years, through loans, shared costs and favours that never come back. You keep enough because your own income keeps rising, and you spend less on proving yourself.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The Horizon at the Year Gate
sections.text: The Horizon stands at your Year Gate, in plain view: your first home spent openly on people and on chances. You grew up in a family that spent on guests, gifts and new plans, and everyone around you could see it. Because money moved freely in the house you grew up in, you learned to spot a chance quickly and to hold cash loosely. That ease with risk has served you all your life, and you have had to build for yourself the savings habit your family never taught.

sections.head: SEAT CARD

sections.text: The Steward lives inside your Year Gate: underneath your first years lay a careful home where nothing was wasted. You took in your family's careful habits with money before you could name them, and they still shape how you feel about spending. Because thrift felt like safety when you were small, you save quietly and early, and your money grows in ways other people mistake for luck. Your relatives remain the people you turn to first, and they turn to you. Under the calm sits a small worry about running short, and you carry it even in good years.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: Your body grows easier to live in with age.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You look after your body through regular meals, gentle movement and people nearby, and it answers you well. Since rest comes easily to you, a good week of it slides into a slow month before you notice. Your health depends more on company than on effort, and you feel the difference within days when you eat alone.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: As a child you were looked after well whenever you were tired or run down, and you got your energy back quickly. By your teens you had a steady energy the adults around you counted on, and you have kept much of it since.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Your appetite and sleep were good in those years, and ordinary pleasures kept you well. You ate with enjoyment and moved without strain, and you felt at ease in your own body.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Since your late forties your sleep has deepened and your appetite has steadied, and you have enjoyed your food without guilt. Your energy has dipped in the stretches when you were on your own too much, and it has come back each time the house filled up again.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: You carry more pressure in these years, and for once it suits your body. You are fitter and sharper in a demanding decade than in an easy one, and you stay that way while you keep sleeping.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: A Sage decade, lining up with the Sage in your Year Gate. It is the stretch that asks most of your body. Too much rest dulls you in these years, and comfort slides into inactivity. Your energy returns through regular movement and a reason to get up early, and you feel better each time you have one.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The Sage inside the Year Gate
sections.text: The Sage lives inside your Year Gate: underneath your childhood was real care, steady enough to trust. Real care sits underneath your early years, from someone whose steadiness became the way you meet the world. Because someone took good care of you, you trust people first, and protectors keep turning up when you need them. The same safety made leaving it hard, and you have stayed in comfortable places longer than they helped you. You still recover from hard seasons by going back to the people who love you.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The Artisan inside the Hour Gate
sections.text: The Artisan lives inside your Hour Gate: your later life settles into good food, deep sleep and people who keep coming back. Your life grows easier with age, and the comfort you have worked for becomes yours to enjoy after your late forties. Because care for you has always meant a good meal and a warm bed, your later home fills with younger people and old friends. Ease is both the reward of those years and their one risk, and you stay well for as long as your days keep a rhythm.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: You are paid to make things better.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You are best in jobs where improving things is the work itself, editing or design or reform of some kind. Because a weak plan is plain to you before anyone asks, you correct work that was never yours to correct. Your value at work grows with every process you improve, and you are known as the colleague who will not let poor work pass.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE · the pair line
sections.text: You do your calmest work closest to pressure, because the deadlines that grind other people turn into steady output in your hands.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: By your teens you were already given responsibility beyond your age, a job at home or a team to lead or younger children to mind. The weight felt heavy at the time, and you came out of it more capable than most of your friends.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Since your late teens you have been handed responsibility early, a budget or a set of keys or a team's accounts. Your promotions have come steadily, each one a little later than your work deserved.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Since your late teens you have been the one who points out what could be better, in a class or a team or a first job. You have clashed with at least one boss over it, and you have also been the person they sent for when something needed fixing.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Your working life in those years was a contest, and you rose by beating others to the same role. You were sharpest with a rival close by, and that edge got you further than talent alone.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: No seat in your Day Gate rules Career. Since your mid-thirties work has taken second place to a partner and your private life, and you have stayed in jobs that ask little of you.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Niche expertise brings offers in these years, through research, advising or technical work. You get paid for knowing what others do not, and your reputation grows inside a small field.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: From your late forties your influence grows as titles start to matter less, and people begin to repeat what you say. Children or younger relatives or someone you train carry your methods into their own work, and you hear your own style in the way they argue with you.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: A General decade, lining up with the General in your Year Gate. It is the stretch that asks most of your work. Demands pile up at work in these years faster than you can meet them, and a calm week feels like falling behind. Your standing survives the decade, and you get through by choosing which fights matter.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Hierarchy presses on you at work in these ten years, and each new duty tightens a frame that is already close. You stay respected throughout, and you find freedom in the parts of the job you shape yourself.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The General at the Year Gate
sections.text: The General stands at your Year Gate, in plain view: from childhood people saw you as someone strong under pressure. Your early life carried pressure that others could see, a demanding home or a tough school or a name you had to defend. Because you were tested young and in public, people learned to respect you early, and authority came to you sooner than to your friends. That start made you hard to push around, and you still meet every new group with your guard up.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The Steward at the Month Gate
sections.text: The Steward stands at your Month Gate, in plain view: at work you are known as the one trusted with the money. People at work hand you the budget, the accounts and the jobs that need order. Because being relied on is how you prove your worth, you take on other people's messes and sort them without fuss. Your income rises on a steady schedule, and your standing rises with it. You are needed everywhere at work, and you are thanked less than you are used.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The Virtuoso inside the Month Gate
sections.text: The Virtuoso holds your strongest seat, inside your Month Gate: your working years run on seeing how everything could be better. You see the better version of almost everything at once, a plan or a process or a piece of work, and your working years are built on that eye. Because a flaw left alone bothers you more than hard work does, you keep improving things long after others call them finished. Managers find you tiring and colleagues find you useful, and you are proud of being both.

sections.head: SEAT CARD
sections.sub: The Virtuoso at the Hour Gate
sections.text: The Virtuoso stands at your Hour Gate, in plain view: your later years are when people hear you most clearly. Your boldest work comes late, after most people expect you to slow down, and it is the work the people after you remember. Because saying the true thing matters more to you than keeping a title, you speak more freely with every year past your late forties, and some who hold rank resent it. Those you teach pick up your talent along with your dislike of being told what to do, and you are proud of both.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: You become the host your family returns to.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: Your home is where your family ends up, for meals and holidays and the nights someone needs a bed. Because a full house makes you feel settled, you take on more hosting than anyone asks of you. Relatives treat your door as always open, and you rarely show them how tired you are by the end.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: As a child you carried a weight in your first home that few people saw, a strict rule or a hard stretch or a worry beyond your age. By your teens you were the steady one in your family, and you kept your own needs to yourself.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Those years made you an equal in your family more than a child or a dependant. You stood on your own feet among your relatives, and they treated your word as worth the same as theirs.

sections.text: From your mid-thirties the family starts to gather at your house, children or relatives or friends who treat it as their second home. Quarrels in the family get settled over your meals, and you become the relative everyone means when they say home.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: From your late forties the people after you, children or younger relatives or someone you train, seek you out for talk they cannot get anywhere else. You become the one in your family whose opinion is asked for, and you give it with more warmth than you once did.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Elders and family support you in these ten years, with advice, practical help or a place to come back to. You receive more care than you expected, and you return it to the people who gave it.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Obligations at home pile up in these years, with duties to elders and a reputation to protect. You meet them faithfully, and you guard a part of your life that belongs to you alone.

sections.text: The General lives inside your Year Gate: underneath your early years was a weight you carried quietly. Because ease makes you feel safe, you look after the people you live with through meals and small comforts more than through words. sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: Your mind never stops improving what it sees.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You think in revisions, turning over a plan or an idea or your own opinion until it is better, and nothing feels quite finished to you. sections.text: Restless thinking ran through those years, and you argued with every idea that came from above. Your mind never settled, and what carried you was one project worth all that energy.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: From your late teens your mind has gone looking for faults, in what you were taught and in what you believed yourself. You have changed your view on something important more than once over those years, and each time you argued yourself into the new view first.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED

sections.text: Intuition sharpens in these ten years, and unusual ideas finally find a use. You think in ways few others do, and people start coming to you for the angle they missed.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: From your late forties your thinking gets bolder, and you say plainly what you held back in earlier years. Your sleep is the part that suffers when an idea grips you, and you sleep well again once you have said it out loud.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Learning comes easily in these years, through books, teachers or a qualification taken at your own pace. Your thinking grows calmer and deeper, and you understand things you once rushed past.

sections.head: TITLE
sections.text: Hard times have always made you grow.

sections.head: HOW YOU ARE
sections.text: You grow fastest when life is hard, and you lose direction when it gets too comfortable. Because difficulty was where you first found your strength, you take on hard projects by choice and feel restless without one. Your best progress comes in the seasons other people would call the worst.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: By your teens you had already learned to rise to a challenge, in school or at home or in a sport. Each hard year left you more capable than before, and you came to trust difficulty more than ease.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Your progress in those years came from peers who were your equals, people you learned beside more than beneath. You set your own standard and met it, and the confidence lasted.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: Private study pays in these years, and the things you taught yourself start to count. You grow in directions nobody planned for you, and the progress shows in work only you could do.

sections.head: COMING

sections.head: TITLE

sections.text: You make your household gentle, with meals shared and voices kept low and nobody left out. Because a peaceful house is what lets you function, you smooth over arguments fast, and some of them never get settled. Your family comes to you to recover from the world, and you let them.

sections.text: As a child you tried new things when someone you trusted stood close by, and you held back when nobody did. By your teens home felt so safe that leaving it seemed harder than staying, and you set off later than your friends.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: Since your late teens you have taught yourself most of what you know, often the slow way. More than once you hit a long flat stretch that ended only when you finally learned from someone better, and you remember each of those people.

sections.head: ALREADY HAPPENED
sections.text: You grew in those years by going your own way, often away from what was expected of you. The progress was real and nearly invisible, and you felt behind while you made it.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: From your late forties you keep learning in public, through new work and through friendships with people much younger than you. You grow more curious with each decade, and you are the one in your family with the newest stories.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: From your late forties your growth comes through company, long talks and shared work with people who expect a great deal of you. You stay sharper in these years than most people your age, and you owe it to the few who keep you honest.

sections.head: COMING
sections.text: You grow fastest in these years through pressure, a hard role or a challenge you choose on purpose. You come out of the decade stronger in the places that used to hold you back.
